newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ferre, Krizia found guilty of corruption.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ferre, Krizia found guilty of corruption.

text.p: An Italian court Friday found top Italian fashion figures Gianfranco Ferre, Krizia and Santo Versace guilty of corruption for paying bribes to tax police.

Ferre, Krizia, whose real name is Mariuccia Mandelli, and Santo Versace, brother and business manager of fashion guru Gianni Versace, each received suspended jail sentences of one year and two months.
Neither Versace, nor designers Krizia and Ferre were in court. Prosecutor Elio Ramondini had asked for 17-month sentences for the three, who had argued they were the victims of corrupt tax officials.
All three have already paid damages roughly equivalent to the amount they paid in bribes in 1990. Ferre handed over the equivalent of $198,000 in bribes, Krizia $260,000 and Versace $163,000.

The trial opened in September 1995 and originally included Milan style guru Giorgio Armani, Krizia's husband Aldo Pinto and Gerolamo Etro, head of the Etro design house, as well as tax inspectors and fashion industry executives.
Armani, Pinto and Etro all plea-bargained and paid damages.
